subject: Numeracy
title: Number stories
objectives: Children will solve simple number stories with objects.
Children will make up a number story.
content: Adding story problems, taking away story problems, and making up our own story.
teachingActivities: Use stories with real objects and children’s own lives (market, school, farm); read each story twice; let children act it out before solving; ask "Do we join or take away?"; keep totals to 5 and extend to 10 for confident children; celebrate different ways of solving.
learnerActivities: Solve simple number stories with objects and make up a number story.
resources: A farm, market and school set
assessment: Observe whether each child solves a story problem to 5 with objects and tells a simple story.
expectedOutcomes: Solves a story problem to 5 with objects.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: working with a partner

lessons.title: Adding stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will solve stories where two groups join together.
successCriteria: Solves an adding story with objects
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join and take away to 5, count to 20 and use money and position words.
lessons.starter: Tell a story: "Three goats are in the field. Two more goats come. How many goats now?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with toy goats.
Join the goats and count all.
Tell a new story for children to solve.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with toy goats. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Join the goats and count all. Children: Children count all the goats.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Three and two make five." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Tell a new story for children to solve. Children: Child solves with objects.

practical.title: Farm adding stories
practical.safety: Use large toy animals and supervise sharing. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Use groups of one, two and three.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to solve a story with a total of ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Did we join or take away?

lessons.conclusion: Put the animals away and say altogether.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell an adding story with toys at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "solve stories where two groups join together" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Taking away stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will solve stories where some are taken away.
successCriteria: Solves a taking away story with objects
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join and take away to 5, count to 20 and use money and position words.
lessons.starter: Tell a story: "Five birds are in the tree. Two fly away. How many birds are left?"
teacherActivities: Act out the story with toy birds.
Take two birds away and count what is left.
Say "Five take away two leaves three."
Tell a new story for children to solve.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Act out the story with toy birds. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Take two birds away and count what is left. Children: Children count the birds left.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Five take away two leaves three." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 4. Teacher: Tell a new story for children to solve. Children: Child solves with objects.

practical.title: Bird stories
practical.safety: Use large toys only and supervise closely. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Use groups of two, three and four.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to solve a story that starts with eight.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Did we join or take away?

lessons.conclusion: Put the birds away and say left.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a taking away story with toys at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "solve stories where some are taken away" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Join or take away?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will decide whether a story is about joining or taking away.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join and take away to 5, count to 20 and use money and position words.
resources: Two baskets: join and take away
lessons.starter: Read two stories and ask "Which story is about joining? Which is about taking away?"
teacherActivities: Read a story and ask whether we join or take away.
Sort story cards into the two baskets.
learnerActivities: Children say join or take away.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Read a story and ask whether we join or take away. Children: Children say join or take away.
Step 2. Teacher: Solve the story with counters. Children: Child solves the story.
Step 3. Teacher: Sort story cards into the two baskets. Children: Child sorts a story card.
Step 4. Teacher: Check the answers together. Children: Children check by counting.

practical.title: Join or take away sort
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a story card for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make up join and take away stories at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "decide whether a story is about joining or taking away" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our own number stories
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make up their own number story and solve a friend’s story.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join and take away to 5, count to 20 and use money and position words.
lessons.starter: Say "Today you are story makers. Make a number story for your friend."
teacherActivities: Show how to make up a story with toys.
Let pairs make a story together.
Let pairs tell their story and ask friends to solve it.
Draw a picture of the story.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to make up a story with toys. Children: Children watch and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Let pairs make a story together. Children: Pairs make a story.
Step 3. Teacher: Let pairs tell their story and ask friends to solve it. Children: Class solves the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Draw a picture of the story. Children: Child draws the story.

practical.title: Story makers
steps: Ask a friend to solve it.
practical.safety: Use large toys only and supervise sharing. Keep crayons away from mouths.

differentiation.support: Make a story together with two toys.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to write the story with numerals.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Display the pictures and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make up number stories with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make up their own number story and solve a friend’s story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 number stories check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child solves and tells number stories.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can join and take away to 5, count to 20 and use money and position words.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: adding, taking away and making a story.
At each station tell a story and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: adding, taking away and making a story. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station tell a story and watch. Children: Child solves with objects.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Story stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large toys. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use totals to three.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to solve a story with totals to ten.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: solves adding stories; solves taking away stories; says join or take away; makes up a story.

questions.question: What is five take away one?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep telling number stories at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child solves and tells number stories" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
